actions.prompt: Workspace: /home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-0.34.0, a git worktree on branch release-0.34.0 that already contains the cost audit under docs/studies/cost-audit-2026-09-18/ (read cost-fix-plan.md section 2 and claude-actual-vs-recorded.md first) and three working transcript readers under scripts/cost-audit/. You edit nothing. Your deliverable is the implementation contract that six parallel writers will build to, so it must be exact and every claim about a provider's data must be proven from real data. Never touch the live ~/.bullswarm: copy it (cp -Rp ~/.bullswarm /tmp/bsw-design) and read the copy. Real data to gather and quote verbatim in the report: (1) Codex stdout: run `codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check -s read-only 'Reply with exactly the word ok' > /tmp/bsw-design/codex-stdout.jsonl 2>/tmp/bsw-design/codex-stderr.txt` in an empty directory, then quote every distinct `type` value and the full `turn.completed` line (or whichever line carries `usage`), so we know which token fields codex reports on stdout (input_tokens, cached_input_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning?) and whether a thread/session id appears (thread.started?). Then find that run's rollout under ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl (match by time), quote its session_meta line and the last event_msg token_count payload.info.total_token_usage object. (2) Grok: quote one real shell.turn.inference_done row from ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl (redact nothing but the prompt text) and state how a bullswarm attempt's session id maps to `sid` (see src/providers/grok/connector.json conversation.newArgs). (3) Claude: quote one real `result` event from a stream-*.jsonl under /tmp/bsw-design/workflows/*/ whose providerType is claude-code (search with grep -l), and state where claude-code transcripts live for a given session id (~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<id>.jsonl and ~/.claude-acme/projects/...; check both) and how the slug is derived from cwd. (4) Meters: read src/meters/framework.js (MeterCache, paceSnapshot, WINDOW_KEYS) and the readUsage exports of src/providers/claude-code/provider.mjs and src/providers/codex/provider.mjs; quote the exact normalized window object shape the cache stores (per-window usedPct, resetsAt, window kind) and how a pool's cached meter is read by name, so the writers can snapshot usedPct at attempt start and end without a network call, and separately how to force a fresh read. Quote the codex WHAM response shape and the claude usage shape as parsed today. (5) Prices: read src/lib/prices.js (priceFor, planPriceFor, subscriptionCostUsd) and quote how a pool's monthly price and plan are resolved today (declared via strategy set-subscription vs detected), and the current rate cards in the three connector.json files. (6) Current record shape: read src/lib/usage.js estimateInvocationUsage, src/lib/watch.js where it is called, src/workflow/v2-dispatch.js where verdict.meta.usage is cloned onto the attempt, src/workflow/v2-runtime.js normalizeAttempt and addUsage, src/workflow/rollup.js pool totals, src/workflow/v2-outcome.js createV2ResultEnvelope, src/workflow/usage-view.js, and the Run/Home/Stats money call sites in src/workflow/dashboard.js and src/workflow/stats-model.js. Then write the contract with these sections, each precise enough to code from without asking: A. attempt.usage v2 record: full field list with types, including tokens {standardRead, cacheRead, cacheWrite5m, cacheWrite1h, cacheWrite, output, reasoning, totalKnown}, tokenSource ladder ('provider-reported' > 'transcript-summed' > 'estimated:utf8-bytes/4' > 'unknown'), sessionId, model, api {usd, breakdown, pricedFields, unpricedFields, rateCard {source, updatedAt}, basis}, subscription {pool, window, deltaPct, usd, monthlyPriceUsd, windowDays, basis in exactly one of 'observed:meter-delta' | 'calibrated:usd-per-pct' | 'unknown:no-price' | 'unknown:no-meter' | 'unknown:no-cost'}, snapshots {start:{at, usedPct, resetsAt}, end:{...}} — and the rule that unknown is null never 0. Keep the existing field names (cost.estimatedUsd, tokens.totalKnown, tokenSource, normalizedQuota) working as aliases so nothing already reading them breaks; say exactly which old fields stay and how they map. B. src/lib/transcripts/: index.js exporting readTranscriptUsage({provider, sessionId, cwd, startedAt, endedAt, home}) that dispatches to claude-code.js, codex.js, grok.js, each exporting the same signature and returning {tokens, model, sessionId, file, firstAt, lastAt, requests, confidence: 'exact'|'window'|'ambiguous'|'none'}; the session-resolution rules per provider (direct id, else cwd + time window; ambiguous → none); the dedup rules to carry over verbatim from scripts/cost-audit (Claude message.id:requestId dedup and subagents/ traversal; Codex last cumulative total_token_usage never summed; Grok per-request sum with the 200K long-context tier). C. The provider hook: each src/providers/<name>/provider.mjs exports `readTranscriptUsage(args)` delegating to the lib module, and the provider loader exposes it; how core discovers it (import the provider module by connector name) and what happens when a provider lacks it. Also the exact eventStream.usage rule JSON for codex (based on the real stdout you captured) and grok (or a statement, with evidence, that grok stdout carries nothing). D. src/lib/subscription-cost.js: windowDays(window) (5h → 5/24, weekly → 7, monthly → calendar days from resetsAt), windowPriceUsd(monthlyPriceUsd, window, resetsAt) = monthlyPriceUsd × windowDays/30.4375 (state the divisor), subscriptionUsdFromPct(pct, windowPriceUsd), the calibration ledger file format at $BULLSWARM_HOME/calibration/<pool>.json ({schema:'bullswarm.calibration.v1', pool, window, samples:[{at, apiUsd, deltaPct, runId, attemptId}], usdPerPct, sampleCount, updatedAt}), how usdPerPct is derived (sum(apiUsd)/sum(deltaPct) over samples with deltaPct > 0, minimum 3 samples before it is used, cap 500 samples), and the decision tree that picks observed vs calibrated vs unknown. E. src/lib/quota-snapshot.js: snapshotPool(poolName, {home}) reading the cached meter only, returning {at, window, usedPct, resetsAt, ageMs} or null; deltaBetween(start, end) handling a reset between the two snapshots (return null with reason) and a stale start; and where in src/lib/watch.js the start snapshot must be taken (before spawn) and the end snapshot (after the process exits, with one forced fresh meter read if the cache is older than 60 s — name the function that forces it). F. Wiring: the exact call sequence in src/lib/watch.js runDelegate → estimateInvocationUsage → transcript fallback (only when tokenSource would be estimated or unknown and a sessionId or cwd+window is known) → subscription attach → calibration append (only when basis is observed and api.usd is known), and what src/cli.js run prints. G. Aggregation: the fields rollup.js adds per pool and per run (apiUsd, subscriptionUsd, measuredAttempts, pricedAttempts, worst tokenSource, worst subscription basis), the same for v2-outcome.js result envelope (per step and total), and the one shared formatter in src/lib/usage-basis.js: formatMoneyPair({api, subscription}) → e.g. '$0.42 api · 1.2% wk ≈ $0.84 sub' with the glyph rule ($ measured, ≈ summed/calibrated, ~ estimated, · unknown) and the exact strings for each basis. H. reprice: `bullswarm workflow reprice [--apply] [--since <date>] [--pool <name>] [--json]` behaviour per attempt, dry-run table format, and the rollup/history rewrite it calls (find reindex in src/workflow/cli.js and name the functions). I. Fixtures: the exact real excerpts (file path + line numbers in the copied home or the provider stores) each writer should copy into tests/fixtures/transcripts/codex-rollout.jsonl, grok-unified.jsonl, claude-session.jsonl, claude-result-event.json, codex-stdout.jsonl, trimmed to under 40 lines each, with the expected totals computed from them so tests can assert real numbers. J. Territory map: confirm for each of the six writers (transcripts, provider-rules, subscription, wiring, views, reprice) that its owned files as listed in the program are sufficient, and list any file that will need an integrator change. Write the whole contract in your final report; it is the only thing the writers will see.

actions.prompt: Workspace: /home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-0.34.0. Judge requirements 1–7 independently from the artifacts, inspecting only; try to break it. Never touch the live ~/.bullswarm: cp -Rp ~/.bullswarm /tmp/bsw-verify and export BULLSWARM_HOME=/tmp/bsw-verify. Run `npm test` and quote the summary. For requirement 1 run `node bin/bullswarm.js run --lane=analyze --add-dir=/tmp/bsw-verify-work --prompt='Reply with the word ok' --json` (mkdir first) and read the saved attempt record: is tokenSource provider-reported or transcript-summed, are the token classes populated, does the number match the provider's own transcript for that session (find it under ~/.codex/sessions or ~/.claude*/projects or ~/.grok/logs and compare)? For 2 check the api block has a per-class breakdown, rate card source and date, and that an unpriced class is named not zeroed; check the cache-write rates in the connectors against their pricingSource pages. For 3 check the subscription block basis strings, that unknown is null not 0, that a meter delta across two snapshots is used when present, and that the calibration ledger under /tmp/bsw-verify/calibration is written only on observed samples with the documented minimum-sample rule. For 4 compare the totals in `workflow runs result --json`, the Run page (`workflow tui --json` or the renderer tests), Home and Stats for one run: do attempt sums equal step sums equal run totals, and does an estimated attempt ever render as a bare $? For 5 run `workflow reprice` dry-run then --apply on the copy and diff a state.json before and after; confirm no-match attempts became unknown with null cost rather than keeping a byte estimate. For 6 run `provider validate` on each connector and read docs/reference/providers.md, docs/guide/cost.md, CHANGELOG.md. For 7 open tests/fixtures/transcripts/ and confirm the fixtures are real excerpts (compare a line against the real store) and the asserted totals follow from them.
